name: Alkem Laboratories Ltd
title: Alkem Laboratories Ltd - 539523 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Alkem's India growth of 10.3% lags peers as Trade Generics stalled (flat in Q1), while Daman US plant OAI and a US CDMO drag of about INR60 crores a quarter weigh on the outlook.

summary.headline: Alkem Q1 FY27 revenue rose close to 11% to INR3,740 crores, but net profit fell 21.7% on tax, and the Daman US plant received an OAI status.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR3,740 crores, up close to 11% YoY, with India at INR2,497 crores (+10.3%) and international at INR1,222 crores (+16%). EBITDA margin was 20.5% (EBITDA up 3.7% YoY), PBT was up about 1.8%, and net profit fell 21.7%, which management attributed to tax. Trade Generics was flat YoY in April-June, which dragged India growth, while branded generics grew about 12%. The Daman facility received an OAI status from the USFDA, which management says has not interrupted supplies.

financial_highlights.value: Improved QoQ and YoY, not quantified

segments.name: India formulations - Trade Generics
segments.commentary: Flat YoY in April-June after higher-single-digit growth in January-June; drag due to tighter receivables/DSO practices, API-linked price increases and competition. Management says it is number 1 or 2 in the segment.

segments.name: India formulations - Branded / non-trade (ex-Trade Generics)
segments.commentary: Branded generics grew about 12%; price up about 6%, new launches about 3%, volume about 2%. Chronic grew 17.9% vs IPM 15.4%; acute grew 12.3% vs IPM 10.1%.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Sales INR1,222 crores, +16% YoY. Management cites Chile, Australia and small high-growth markets such as Germany (35-40% growth) as drivers.

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: Management described US as challenging with little volume growth and near-flat price erosion; FY27 US guidance now high single digit to mid, helped by currency. Daman plant supplies about 45% of US revenue.

segments.name: MedTech (Occlutech and ortho)
segments.commentary: Occlutech acquisition completed mid-July, so no Q1 impact; ex-diligence, Q1 EBITDA loss of about INR5-7 crores from ortho/MedTech. FY27 target about INR400 crores sales for the roughly 8.5 months of ownership with breakeven EBITDA.

segments.name: US CDMO (Enzene, mAbs)
segments.commentary: Operating cost about INR60 crores per quarter; breakeven needs about USD25-30 million annualised revenue, now expected in FY28, with capex needed later and no US FDA approval yet on the facility.

guidance_outlook: US revenue growth now guided at high single digit to mid for FY27, versus earlier high single digit, with currency support.
India growth for the full year about 1 percentage point better than the prior guidance, which management put at close to 12%.
Gross margin guidance of 66.5%-67% maintained for the balance of FY27, with API price increases expected to weigh in later quarters.
Consolidated tax rate guided at 30%-32% (standalone earlier 27%-28%), because loss-making entities such as US Enzene carry no deferred tax asset.
Occlutech FY27 target about INR400 crores sales with breakeven EBITDA; EBITDA margin improving 7-8% YoY and reaching guidance over 3-4 years.
US CDMO expected to break even in 4-5 quarters per CFO, but MD later said it will not break even within 12 months; Trade Generics growth expected to recover to late single digits.
Denosumab biosimilar US approval delayed by at least a few months; Xgeva biosimilar EU launch about 3 months away; Tolvaptan US generic launch expected this quarter.
capex_capacity: Daman US facility received OAI status; corrective and preventive actions initiated, resolution expected in 6-12 months; 45% of US revenue comes from Daman.

Enzene US CDMO (mAbs, development to clinical supplies) operational since November 2025; capacity described as small but technologically differentiated; not yet US FDA approved; capex will be needed later, not this year.
Added about 1,200 MRs over the last few quarters, adding to employee cost.
Backward integration into 7 biosimilars in India generating about INR150 crores annual sales, with improved margins.
Acquisition of Occlutech completed mid-July 2026; integration started, with more India-operations integration expected from next quarter.
demand_pricing: India Trade Generics competition has intensified as large players entered; company also tightened receivable days, slowing primary sales.
Price in India ex-Trade Generics up about 6% YoY; US price erosion close to flat, which management says may have bottomed out.
Semaglutide going off patent is driving chronic market growth; Alkem's benefit so far is very small.
Gross margin improved on lower Trade Generics mix, stronger prescription business and currency; API price increases will weigh on later quarters.
Outperformed IPM in 7 focus therapies: anti-infectives 1.1x, gastro 1.2x, vitamins and minerals 1.4x, pain 1.8x, antidiabetic 1.4x, respiratory 1.6x, derma 1.6x.
Five US ANDA approvals in the quarter, one of them tentative.

qa_highlights.question: Why is India growth (10.3%) below most peers, and will it ease?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the drag to Trade Generics, which was flat to mildly up; branded generics grew about 12%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the cost increase is from CDMO and MedTech, and what are the losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost rose more than 16% from increments, about 1,200 added MRs and Enzene CDMO becoming operational in November 2025; US CDMO opex is about INR60 crores per quarter; ex-Occlutech MedTech losses are about INR5-7 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Trade Generics outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was flat in April-June after higher-single-digit growth in January-June; management expects recovery, and personally would be happy with late single digits over the next 1-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Occlutech outlook and margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 target of about INR400 crores sales with breakeven EBITDA for about 8.5 months; the earlier 10% margin guidance is pushed out, reaching guidance over 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: How much of US revenue depends on the Daman plant, and are supplies affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Daman accounts for about 45% of US revenue; management says supplies continue without interruption and the impact is not expected this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate and US outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated tax rate is 30-32% because loss-making entities carry no deferred tax asset; US growth guided at high single digit to mid, helped by currency and not volume.

risks_watch: Daman OAI status: resolution timeline 6-12 months, and whether it affects US supplies or new ANDA approvals; company has 45% of US revenue from this plant.
Trade Generics: whether growth recovers to late single digits as receivables discipline and API-driven price rises play out.
API price increases pressuring gross margin in the coming quarters against the 66.5%-67% guidance.
US CDMO: lumpy contract timing, USD25-30 million annualised breakeven, and FY28 revenue timeline.
Net profit fall of 21.7% and the 30-32% consolidated tax rate; watch for deferred tax asset recognition.
Denosumab biosimilar US approval delay; CEO hire still pending.
summary.management_tone: Confident on India branded and international growth, but cautious and somewhat evasive on Trade Generics, US CDMO timelines and the Daman OAI, where answers were often qualified or deferred.
key_quotes: While this represents an important regulatory development, approved product supplies from the facility continue to the U.S. market without any interruption.
So next 12 months will not breakeven, just to be very clear. For U.S., we will not breakeven.
So we maintain the same guidance of 66.5% to 67% of gross margins for balance part of the year.

adds.what: Occlutech acquisition (MedTech) completed mid-July 2026; acquired, not company-built capacity
Enzene US CDMO (mAbs) facility, operational since Nov 2025, small, not US FDA approved; capex needed later, not this year
Backward integration into 7 biosimilars in India generating about INR150 crores annual sales

growth.why: India growth guided close to 12% for FY27 (about 1 pt above prior), US cut to high single digit to mid, with price, branded growth (~12%), share gains (13.2% vs IPM 12.2%) and international (+16%) as drivers; no new capacity quantified and US Daman plant under OAI, so backing is partial.
